name: arctic
title: Iceberg in victor bay, arctic bay.JPG
author: Slp1
notes: Commons description: 'Iceberg in Victor Bay, near Arctic Bay, Nunavut, Canada' (northern Baffin Island), September 2006; author's own work released into the public domain (Commons tag PD-self). Film scan 3089x2048 used as-is (no downscale) and uploaded to Canva unchanged. Canva remove-background kept only the floating iceberg cluster (5 ice pieces plus the submerged turquoise ice between them; one clean alpha component, bbox x873-1974 y853-1239 = 1102x387 px of 3089x2048); water, beach/surf, cliffs, haze and sky removed. Exported from the layered design as transparent lossless PNG 3089x2048 (pro) = near layer (fg). Far plate (bg) 2400x1591: first built with scripts/make_plate.py (kept as assets-src/tmp-arctic/arctic-bg_plate_makeplate_v1.jpg), but its TELEA fill left a visible blurry halo around the iceberg, so the delivered plate uses the same idea with a tighter mask and a texture-preserving fill (row-wise low-frequency interpolation + water/film texture copied from the same rows; script assets-src/tmp-arctic/py/refine_plate2.py); only pixels within 50 px of the iceberg differ from the photo. Checked plate + fg aligned and fg shifted +/-40 px at plate scale: clean water and shoreline revealed, no ghost. To align, scale fg 3089->2400 wide (same aspect); fg bbox at plate scale x678-1534 y663-963. Depth caveat: the beach/surf strip at the bottom (below ~y1250 of the 2400x1591 plate) is physically nearer than the iceberg but lives in the bg plate, so keep the parallax gentle or frame that strip out. First attempt (Navy Board Inlet glacier snout, CC BY 2.0 Mike Beauregard, Canva media MAHaX3zRbW4) was rejected by Canva remove-background: 'No clear foreground subject'. No people, text or aircraft in frame.
